comment: If you're looking for an easy A in Calc 2, she is the professor to take. You can repeat quizzes up to 3 times to get a "pass" on that specifc quiz. and each is quiz is 1 question each although some go up to 3. If you don't get an A in this class, then it's on you because she makes it very easy

Prof Torres uses a mastery based style of grading, so everyone can retake quizzes they don't do well on the first time, which is nice and helpful for learning. However, you do a lot of the learning through the homework instead of in class and when you are confused she can feel condescending at times.

I have no words for this professor. I have never met a woman who is so condescending toward her students. Just because she had A's in college after getting a C in pre-calc doesn't mean we should all be compared to the same standards. Real happy these 2 semesters are over, never looking back.
It's hard to pay attention in class. She does not go deep in the subject and only grade based on a few things.

A very unprofessional and condescending professor, she laughs at students when they can't grasp the material. Honestly, I have never met someone ruder. Take her if you don't mind being laughed at. I think the only good thing about her class was the fact that she did allow retakes on quizzes; besides that, it was terrible.

The grading scale is mastery based which has its pro's and con's. You have to watch alot of youtube videos to actually understand the topics. Its very easy to pass her class, just make sure you do the homework and guided studies. Also, make sure to come to class on time because attendence does matter.

Her grading system is great. But she is a lot of the time very rude and condescending to students. You can tell she really cares and puts a ton of effort into doing all the math problems and explaining them, but somehow she does so in the most convoluted unnecessarily confusing way. I would recommend her only if you've taken calc before.

The mastery-based grading system of this class makes it very easy to do well. By the end of the semester, if your grade is high enough you dont even need to show up to class anymore or even take the final. Torres is a nice, relaxed teacher but she doesnt teach the content very well. Most of the learning is online, and class is just group work.

She uses the Mastery grading system which, at first, seems really confusing but it makes it really easy to get a good grade. You dont have to do the homework to understand the class but do it if you want a good grade. Would recommend taking for credit.

Torres is great. I had her for Calc 1 and 2 and the class is very easy to do well in if you do the minimal work she assigns. You mostly learn through videos online, so you have to do the homework to understand the classwork. Tests have cheat sheets and can be retaken multiple times. You HAVE to go to class, participation is a huge part of the grade

Dr. Torres is a good professor. Her classes are well-structured, a lot of individual work, grading is fair; gives you a lot of attempts for A. However, I felt I'm teaching everything to myself. The class is based on group projects: usually annoying and overwhelming. Her attitude makes you feel dumb when asking questions. No understanding or care.

I had Dr. Torres for Calc I and II. She uses a mastery based grading system so as long as you try you will get an A in the class. I think if you are passionate about math or care to learn it well, you will be able to learn the concepts from the videos provided. The classroom is flipped so you learn online then apply concepts in class.

She uses the "metric grading system", which makes it extremely clear and easy to know what is expected from you for a specific grade. Before every class, she assigns 'guided studies', which are basically YouTube videos teaching the upcoming topic. In class, you just practice problems - she barely teaches. Quizzes are biweekly. Do the work  Easy A
Shes awful in general. Work is rudimentary expects you to learn on your own. Has no communication skills with students at all.

My thoughts: She teaches through videos and lectures that are not personalized to the class nor her own. Does not make an effort to actually communicate with students or empathize in the midst of a pandemic. Hope this helped.

Dr. Torres is very is very knowledgable on the subject however, it seems like she doesn't know how to teach it. During class, she would read off slides and we would be split into groups to fill out worksheets. They were no help at all when it came time to do the homework which was based on a concept taught through videos from another school.

Dr. Torres is a wonderful professor and she truly cares about her students and their education. The rubric is very clear on the expectations to receive a grade. Instead of giving students a bad grade, she cares more about them fully understanding the concepts and gives them an option to retake quizzes . Also, work is graded and returned quickly!

Dr. Torres is a a fairly good professor, and she does make receiving an A in the class fairly easy with her option of taking retakes. But, If your math classes were solely computational and barely conceptual, this might not be the class for you. She does integrate a lot of applications, but I just wanted a math class that had me plug and chug.
